hook_text: Four companies, twelve sketches, clipboards out. Here is how engineers review a design without a fist fight.
clip_script: Every real design is reviewed before it is built, by people who did not design it, because they see what you cannot. Rules: judge each sketch against that company's own specifications, not your taste. Score each rule 0 to 3. No talking; the sketch must speak. Score alone, then agree. Sign it. Write three lines: strongest feature, biggest risk, one suggestion. Phrase it against the rule: not 'this falls over' but 'no diagonals on the side face, so sway is not met.' Then it is your turn to be reviewed. Read every sheet before you argue. Sort: agree, disagree with reasons, check. If three reviewers name the same risk, it is real. The sting that is right is the best line you will get. Then choose, in a written note: totals, spread, three reasons, borrowed features, accepted risks. Not a vote. Not whose sketch it was. Reasons a board can follow.
visual_style: Four whiteboard stations with pinned sketches; clipboards score 0-3 down a list; three written lines appear; a company sorts sheets into three piles; a decision note writes itself with totals and reasons.
mood: Professional, fair, a little tense then resolved.
pacing: The rules, scoring, phrasing, receiving, deciding.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and write one specification-based criticism of your own best sketch before anyone else does.
